# <span id="aanchor128"></span> Gas Quality Source Editor

## Characteristic Tab

The Characteristic tab is used to configure and manage the behavior and functionality for how FLOWCAL acts on quality samples as it pertains to imports, calculations, rollups, and other aspects. The characteristics are datetime effective and can be modified as needed to properly handle changes in quality sampling.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Char 1">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Characteristic 1 Sub-Tab</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Char 1">



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 561;height: 491;" />

The Characteristics 1 sub-tab contains the following items:

- **Status** - Current status of the quality source; may be "In Service", "Temporarily Out", or "Permanently Out".

  Source message 302 ("Source status changed") is generated when users update this field.

- **Type** - See: [About Sources](../../Sources/About%20Sources.md)
  - **Sample Analysis** - Used if quality samples are spot samples or composite lab samples.

  - **Chromatograph** - Used if quality samples come from an online chromatograph. The type must be set to Chromatograph for the gas quality source hourly and daily reports to be run.

    When the "Enable Rollups" option is checked, and the type is "Chromatograph" or "RTU Average", the quality samples are averaged and rolled up into daily and monthly averages. Sample pressure and sample temperature are not rolled up for chromatographs. If the type is "Gas Analysis", the quality is copied directly to the rollup tables.

<!-- -->

- **C6+ Split** - C6+ splits provide for the C(n)+ properties to be calculated from a fixed ratio of pure component (C6 through C10) properties. You can specify how a C6+ value is to be split for calculating HCDP, CCT, gravity, heating value, and liquid content (GPMs).

- **C7+ Split** - C7+ splits provide for the C(n)+properties to be calculated from a fixed ratio of pure component (C7 through C10) properties. You can specify how a C7+ value is to be split for calculating HCDP, CCT, gravity, heating value, and liquid content (GPMs).

- **Contract Day/Hour** - Contract day and hour can be specified if a source is enabled for rollups. These are used to calculate logical measurement months and measurement days for source rollup purposes.

- **Pressure Base** - Default sample pressure base.

- **Temperature Base** - Default sample temperature base.

- **Atm. Pressure** - Default atmospheric pressure.

- **Z Method** - Calculation method for gas compressibility. This applies to gas quality sources only. Available options are:

  - AGA-8 Detail (1992)
  - AGA-8 Details (2017)
  - AGA-8 GERG (2017)
  - Fpv = 1.0

  If you do not select a Z-method from the drop-down, FLOWCAL will default to AGA-8 Detail (1992).

- **Replace Imported Values with Calculated Results** - By default, FLOWCAL will calculate all possible sample properties from the imported components’ mole percent. FLOWCAL will save the calculated value for any property not provided in the import file. When this option is enabled, FLOWCAL will also replace the properties that have been included in the import file, such as molar mass, densities, Wobbe index, and heating values.

- **Component Characterization Method** - Determines how the C(n)+ fluid properties are calculated when a sample is only analyzed to C6 (or to C7, C8, etc.). Enabling the "Use Extended Characteristics" option allows the C(n)+ properties to be calculated from a full characterization of the C(n)+ portion of the sample. This can be imported via text file or manually entered.

  Manual entry is only supported for C6+ properties.

- **Characterization Date** - Records of the C6+ characterization effective date of the extended characteristics; this is a read-only field. Characteristic records may be split in time for any of various reasons. Each split will have its own effective date. The characterization date only changes when the extended characteristics change.

  BLM requires either a C9 analysis or a C6+ characterization when the C6 component exceeds 0.5 mole percent. If a characterization is used, it must be updated at intervals that depend on the FMP's volume tier. FLOWCAL uses this characterization date to know the "age" of the current characterization and to provide a warning (in the form of an exception) when the interval date is approaching.

  The value is generally equal to the source characteristic's effective date (also visible on that screen) but there are manual entry and "out-of-order" import scenarios that will cause that date to differ. It may be considered an FYI value as it is FLOWCAL's best attempt to notify the user as noted above and is not a BLM-required reporting field.

- **Reason** - An edit reason must be entered when a new source is created, or a source is edited.

- **User Name** - User that made the most recent change to the source.

</div>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Char 2">



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 573;height: 502;" />

The Characteristics 2 sub-tab contains the following items:

- **Custom Fields** - Ten custom fields are available. The first five are numeric and the next five are alphanumeric with a 50-character limit. The labels can be user-defined by the administrator (see also Custom Fields).

- **Associated GQ Source, Sample Interval, and Instrument Inspection** - This feature is no longer supported and is not tied to any functionality.

- **Notes** - These notes are associated to the source characteristic record.

  The notes stored on the Characteristic 2 tab are only available from the Gas Quality Source Editor. Right-click the top of the Gas Quality Source Editor screen to add or view notes that can be accessed throughout the application (e.g., from the Source Analysis Rollup Viewer).

</div>

Use the Ext (Extended) Combinations tab to view the imported, calculated, or edited values of each possible C(n)+ combination, whether based on an analysis of the C(n)+ portion of the sample or a defined component C6+/C7+ split fixed ratio.
